description:
Advances: ancora.derive

Wave 1 of ancora-gg8 (investigation record and architecture decision live as comments there). Original finding below the fold; the shape is now decided per the gg8 architecture decision (findings-B, B3).

Deliverable:
Normalize lib_paths once at load time in ProjectInfo.validate_lib_paths/1 (lib/ancora/project_info.ex:138-147) — trim trailing slashes there, since every source of lib_paths funnels through it (explicit opts, .spec/config.yml, elixirc_paths fallback). Then delete the trim in ChangeAnalysis.under_lib_path?/2 (lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex:30-35) so exactly one place owns normalization. This kills the whole class, including the subtler defect: ModuleLocator's strict source_path?/2 (lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex:155-160) drops changed base sources under a trailing-slash lib_path, so base and head module sets diverge for reasons unrelated to the diff, contaminating drift/growth/shrink comparison — not just footprints. Do NOT fix by trimming in source_path?/2 too; single-point normalization is the decided shape (a shared boundary helper is optional style, not required scope).

Spec delta (land in this same diff):
Append one sentence to the `ancora.derive.project_info_from_root` statement: "Every `lib_paths` value shall be normalized at resolution — trailing slashes trimmed — so all downstream path comparisons use one canonical form." Add a scenario `ancora.derive.scenario.trailing_slash_lib_path` — given `lib_paths: ["src/"]` and a changed, TAGGED source at src/thing.ex, when the gate runs, then the file enters its subject's footprint and no change/uncovered_file fires.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: new tagged test pinning the trailing-slash case with a TAGGED file (the "cannot be cleared" half is what must fail on regression — an untagged file cannot distinguish the two code paths; see the auditor note below). Existing derive/change_analysis suites.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: ancora.derive.scenario.trailing_slash_lib_path; base/head membership identical for an unchanged tree regardless of trailing slash in config.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe tmp-repo fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: no new callable surface; validate_lib_paths/1 is already on the preflight path.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex
- lib/ancora/severity.ex
- lib/ancora/output*.ex

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/project_info.ex
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex
- test/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (the statement sentence and scenario above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No shared under_path?/2 helper extraction unless it falls out for free — normalization at the funnel is the fix
- No behavior change for lib_paths without trailing slashes
- No config-parse rejection of trailing slashes (declined on the epic)

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

--- Original finding (preserved) ---

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Found by the cold auditor on the ancora-p47 stack; it corrects a claim the cold verifier got wrong.

Concrete failure: with lib_paths: ["src/"] (a trailing slash, which the config schema accepts), a changed and TAGGED source file at src/thing.ex is reported as change/uncovered_file and the finding can never be cleared, because the file can never enter any subject footprint.

Mechanism: the two places that decide "is this path under a lib_path" disagree about trailing slashes.
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex under_lib_path?/2 (added by ancora-p47) does String.trim_trailing(lib_path, "/") before comparing, so "src/" matches src/thing.ex and the gate considers the file in scope.
- lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex:155 source_path?/2 does NOT trim, so with "src/" it never recognises src/thing.ex as a source, never indexes it, and the file never lands in a footprint.
Nothing upstream normalises: String.trim_trailing appears exactly once in all of lib/, in the new helper. The result is a finding that fires and cannot be silenced by doing the thing the finding asks for.

Why it was not caught earlier: the cold verifier asserted that a trailing-slash config "behaves identically", but its experiment used an UNTAGGED file, which is flagged under either code path, so the experiment could not distinguish them. Recording that because the mistake is instructive: an experiment that produces the same output for both hypotheses is not evidence for either.

Not a defect in ancora-p47 and deliberately not bounced there: source_path?/2 predates that ticket and is outside its Allowed touches. Proving the end-to-end false positive needs a gate run with a tagged source under a trailing-slash lib_path, which the read-only auditor could not perform.

Fix direction: make source_path?/2 trim trailing slashes, or better, collapse both call sites onto one shared boundary helper so the rule exists in exactly one place. The auditor recommended the shared helper. A test should pin the trailing-slash case specifically, with a TAGGED file, so the "cannot be cleared" half is what fails if it regresses.

Cannot land on the ancora-p47 stack: out of scope there, and the shared-helper shape is a small design decision rather than a mechanical edit.
